STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Greater one-horned rhinoceros
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The rhino is the living emblem of Assam's wild grasslands.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The Indian rhinoceros is inseparably tied to Kaziranga National Park, which protects a large share of the world's wild population. A symbol of survival, it draws visitors to the Brahmaputra floodplains. Classified Vulnerable by the IUCN, it remains a global conservation priority.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: White-winged wood duck
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: A rare forest waterfowl of Assam's evergreen wetlands.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The white-winged duck — or deohah — is a large, secretive duck of Assam's tropical evergreen forests and slow rivers, seen at Nameri and the foothill wetlands. Dark-bodied with a striking whitish head, it is among the most endangered waterfowl in the world, listed Critically Endangered by the IUCN and protected under CITES Appendix I.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Foxtail orchid (Kopou phul)
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The bloom that heralds Rongali Bihu across the state.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The Kopou phul, with its fragrant, densely packed purple-white inflorescences, is woven into the hair of Bihu dancers each spring. Symbolising love, joy and renewal, it is the floral emblem of Assam — its appearance marks the arrival of the Assamese new year.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Hollong
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The royal hardwood of Assam's evergreen forests.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Hollong is a tropical hardwood found in Assam's evergreen and semi-evergreen forests. It is an important part of the state's forest ecosystems and conservation heritage.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Kaji Nemu (Assam lemon)
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The GI-tagged lemon declared the state fruit in 2024.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Kaji Nemu is a lemon variety associated with Assam. It was declared the state fruit in 2024 and has Geographical Indication status; it is used as a condiment and in drinks and dishes.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Bihu
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: A major festival cycle linked to seasonal and agricultural life in Assam.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The three Bihus are Rongali (Bohag) in spring, Kongali (Kati) during the growing season and Bhogali (Magh) after the harvest. Their customs vary by community and place; music, dance, food and seasonal observances are central to many celebrations.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Bihu Dance
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: A widely recognized folk dance tradition associated with Bihu celebrations.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Bihu dance is performed to rhythms including the dhol and pepa. Costumes, choreography and performance styles vary; it is one of Assam's best-known cultural traditions.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: O Mur Apunar Dekh
STATE_SYMBOLS.official: অ' মোৰ আপোনাৰ দেশ — 'O My Endearing Country'
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The beloved state anthem of Assam.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Written by Lakshminath Bezbaroa — the great Assamese poet and novelist — 'O Mur Apunar Dekh' is Assam's official state song. Sung at the start of every official function and assembly, its opening words are a love-letter to the land: 'O my endearing country, the land of red hills and blue rivers.'

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Joi Aai Axom
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: A popular expression of pride and belonging.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: 'Joi Aai Axom' means 'Hail Mother Assam' and is widely used as a slogan expressing Assamese pride. It is not an official state motto.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Assamese
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: One of Assam's official languages, written in the Assamese script.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: Assamese (Axomiya) is one of Assam's official languages. Bodo, Bengali and many Indigenous languages are also spoken across the state, with language use varying by region and community.

STATE_SYMBOLS.name: Emblem of Assam
STATE_SYMBOLS.why: The official seal carried on the state's correspondence.
STATE_SYMBOLS.detail: The state seal of Assam is carried on the official correspondence of the Government of Assam and listed on the state's portal as the 'State Seal'. Assam does not have an officially recognised flag; instead a banner displaying the state seal on a plain field represents the Government of Assam.
